ranked.mechanism: Friction-induced velocity-weakening instability in rolling contact, where increased static friction coefficient at low temperatures causes a drop in available torque below the threshold required to maintain rotational equilibrium.
ranked.intervention: Implement a thermal management loop using a Joule-heated bearing housing to maintain the grease fluidity coefficient above the critical shear-thinning threshold during shadow periods, preventing the transition from fluid lubrication to boundary lubrication.

ranked.mechanism: Spherical reaction wheel geometry eliminating fixed-axis bearing preload variation
ranked.intervention: Replace the conventional cylindrical rotor and paired angular-contact bearings with a spherical rotor supported by a symmetric multi-point bearing arrangement to decouple differential thermal contraction from bearing preload.

ranked.mechanism: The intermittent stall at low temperature is caused by a thermal-induced increase in bearing friction that exceeds the available control moment, effectively creating a static constraint that locks the wheel; this is analogous to the "limits on control moments" and "constrained RW desaturation" mechanism where the control authority is bounded by physical limits, causing the system to fail when the demand for desaturation or attitude correction exceeds the available torque margin at that operating point.
ranked.intervention: Implement an incremental reference governor strategy that proactively limits the demanded wheel speed and control moment to stay within the reduced thermal torque capability, thereby preventing the wheel from driving into the high-friction stall region where the bearing friction locks the rotor.

ranked.mechanism: Frictional torque in the wheel bearings scales exponentially with temperature drop due to standard lubricant viscosity increase and boundary layer thinning, reducing bearing life and increasing stiction. At low temperatures, the increased torque exceeds the minimum drive current capability of the motor, causing intermittent stalls when attitude control demand is low or zero, resulting in attitude drift.
ranked.intervention: Select a lubricant with lower baseline viscosity and a lower viscosity-temperature coefficient (e.g., synthetic ester or PAO-based grease with low-temperature additives) and verify the temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) of the stator windings at low temperature to ensure drive current scales appropriately with the increased back-EMF.
